critique: The bioluminescent jade-and-coral jellyfish, crowned with gold ziggurat crests and beaded tentacles, fuse marine life with Art Deco architecture in a bold, delightfully strange underwater metropolis. The rigid chevron bands, frame, skyline, sunburst, newt plaque, date stamp, and tiny guinea-pig cameo create too many competing motifs; enlarging and integrating the animal glyphs into the architecture while muting one or two ornamental layers would give the drifting jellyfish greater visual authority.
